newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash LPG prices surge on tight stocks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash LPG prices surge on tight stocks.

text.p: U.S. spot LPG prices were narrowly mixed late Friday, as bullish crude futures and supply concerns were offset by thin pre-weekend trade.
"The strength is on the NYMEX and the nervousness over the lack of imports," one Houston-based trader said.
Cargoes have slackened because high European prices are keeping products overseas.
And that added to upward pressure as stocks continue at historic lows before high winter consumption begins.
Propane prices were flat at 42.50/42.75 cents a gallon at Mont Belivieu, Texas, traders said. Normal Butane edged up 0.25 cent to reach 50.50/50.75 cents a gallon.
Isobutane slipped 0.25 cent 52.50/52.75 cents a gallon.
Propane at Conway, Kansas, was pegged at 41.25 cents a gallon, up about one quarter-cent from Thursday.
A 15,000 barrel parcel of Conway propane was heard done at 42 cents.
-- Franklin Paul, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
